$comment: R-CONSUMED — the ONE consumption rule, two implementations (brick e09628a1, CONCEPTION §3 / §6.1). Authored in acpx (test/fixtures/delivery-consumption.fixture.json) and vendored BYTE-IDENTICALLY into acpx-ui at the same path; both suites assert the same sha256 over these bytes and run every vector — acpx feeds the frames one by one through ConsumptionTracker (src/session/delivery-consumption.ts), acpx-ui runs classifyStreamConsumption (server/delivery-consumption.ts) over the batch. A one-sided edit reds a suite. DO NOT REFORMAT: the sha is over the file bytes. Frames are REAL stream frames trimmed to the fields the rule reads (text shortened, sessionId and tool payloads dropped; a run of consecutive text chunks of one kind collapsed to its first frame); each names its source session and line. Regenerate with conception/evidence tooling only from real streams — never hand-edit a frame.

classification.$comment: A model-output frame is a session/update whose sessionUpdate is in outputSessionUpdates, except an agent_message_chunk whose text equals excludedAgentMessageText. tool_call_update is NOT output. A completion frame is a session/update with sessionUpdate completionSessionUpdate carrying _meta[completionMetaKey]. A completion counts only if a model-output frame lies between it and the previous counted completion (or the prompt frame). Counting for a message stops at its first terminal acpx/delivery frame (terminalDeliveryPhases), even one written before its prompt frame.

note.$comment: Every consumption-aware done carries error {code:0, message:"<prefix>: <cause>", detailCode:<the code the old path would have written>} as a non-failing note. Neither the prefix nor any cause may contain a forbidden substring (lower-cased): acpx-ui reads those as a close.
